verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā bhikkhū, kosalesu viharanti himavantapasse araññakuṭikāya uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā muṭṭhassatino asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā pākatindriyā.
verses.english: At one time several mendicants were staying in the Kosalan lands, in a wilderness hut on the slopes of the Himalayas. They were restless, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

verses.pali: Atha kho jantu devaputto tadahuposathe pannarase yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then on the fifteenth day sabbath the godling Jantu went up to those mendicants and addressed them in verse:
Knowing that the world was impermanent
they made an end of suffering.
But now they’ve made themselves hard to look after,
They eat and eat and then lie down,
passed out in the homes of others.
Having raised my cupped palms to the Saṅgha,
I speak here only about certain people.
just like those who have passed away.
